instructions: Pour the 5 cups broth into a saucepan and set it over low heat so it's warm when you need it.
Meanwhile, peel the squash, scoop out the seeds and cut it into 1/2 inch cubes. That should be about 3 cups.
Finely chop the onion and mince the 2 garlic cloves. Pick 12 whole sage leaves and set them aside, then mince 1 tsp of the sage. Finely grate the Parmesan.

Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large, wide pot over medium heat. When it foams, add the 12 sage leaves in one layer and fry them for 1 to 2 minutes, until they're crisp and a shade darker. Transfer them onto a paper towel.
Add the 2 tbsp olive oil to the same pot. Add the onion, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft.
Add the squash and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the edges start to turn golden and a knife goes in with a little push.
Add the garlic and the minced sage and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Add the rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges of the grains look see-through.
Pour in the 1/2 cup wine and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the pot looks almost dry.

Add a ladle of the warm broth, about 3/4 cup, and stir often until the rice has soaked almost all of it up, 2 to 3 minutes. Keep adding broth a ladle at a time, letting each one soak in before the next. After 20 to 25 minutes the rice should be creamy and tender with a little bite left in the middle. Some of the squash will break down into the rice and turn it golden. You may not need all the broth.

Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp butter, the Parmesan and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. If it's stiff, stir in a splash of the broth. It should slowly spread out when you spoon it onto a plate.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the crisp sage leaves crumbled over the top.
method_notes: Both versions build a classic risotto on Arborio, a splash of dry white wine and warm broth added a ladle at a time, finished with Parmesan and sage. Love and Lemons cooks the squash cubes in the pot with the onion before the rice goes in, uses vegetable broth and keeps the cheese optional. Well Plated roasts the squash separately at 400°F, adds bacon and chicken stock, and stirs the squash in at the end with butter and sage. This follows Love and Lemons so the dish stays vegetarian and some of the squash melts into the rice, with Well Plated's butter and Parmesan finish and the sage leaves fried crisp for the top.
